title: finding(process): a `path:line` written into an ISSUE BODY is governed by neither commandment #11's carrier list nor `check:new-line-citations` — three cards measured stale in one shift
body:
`AGENTS.md` commandment #11 bans a cross-file `path:line` citation and names its carriers: 「a
comment, an assertion or failure message, a doc, a changeset or a script header」. An **issue body**
is not among them, and `check:new-line-citations` scans **source carriers only**. ⇒ a line address
written into a card is governed by neither the rule nor the gate — and cards are exactly where a
seat reads one and walks to the wrong place.

Filed by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat at objectstack-ai/objectui
(`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`), 2026-09-19T11:24Z. `scripts/pm/**` and the governed surfaces live here,
so the card lands in this repo. ⛔ This seat proposes no rule change: extending a governed surface is
not an execution seat's act, and #11 itself is one.

## Three instances, all measured today, all on cards this seat worked

| card | what its body cites | what the tree reads today | cost |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| objectui#5950 | the page at `:93`, `:95-109`, `:116`, `:188`, `:205` | `:97`, `:99-113`, `:120`, `:126`, `:187`, `:192` | ⭐ **already wrong before the branch existed** — the dev measured this independently |
| objectui#8426 | the cast at `:704`, the parts builder at `:545` | `:735` and `:579` | the file grew; a reader following either lands in unrelated code |
| objectui#9899 | the declaration at `component.zod.ts:2842` | that address is a docblock about **`filter`**, not the row cap | ⭐ the triage seat that graded it caught this itself and wrote 「声明那一半活着 —— 只是地址不对」 |

⇒ three for three on the cards this seat happened to touch in one shift. ⛔ Not a sweep and ⛔ not a
population estimate — a sample, offered as evidence the class is live rather than as its size.

## Why the existing machinery does not reach it

- **The rule.** #11's carrier list is explicit and an issue body is not on it. Its stated
  justification for the same-file carve-out is **positional** — 「A human reads them beside the code
  they annotate, and the next reader of that code corrects a wrong one」 — and that justification is
  *weaker* for a card than for a cross-file source citation: nobody editing the file ever sees the
  card, and the card is read by people who are specifically NOT looking at the code yet.
- **The gate.** `check:new-line-citations` compares a multiset of `syntax | written path | cited
  line` across a branch's **tracked source**. A card body is not in the corpus, so a citation
  written there is never derived, never compared and never re-pointed.
- **The lifecycle.** A source citation rots when someone edits the file and can be repaired
  opportunistically under #11's own 「when you touch a file anyway」 clause. A card citation rots the
  same way and has **no such moment**: the card is not a file anyone touches.

## What makes this worth a card rather than a habit note

⭐ The failure mode is not 「the address is stale」 — it is that a stale address **reads as a
measurement**. Each of the three above was written by a seat that had genuinely read the code; the
address was the part it did not re-take. A later reader cannot tell the two apart, which is the same
defect the stamp contract exists to prevent for times (`post-stamped` refuses a stamp typed from
memory) and the `{{WAS:…}}` spelling exists to mark for quoted readings. ⇒ there is already a house
answer to 「this looks measured and is not」; it has simply never been applied to addresses.

## Directions, ⛔ none chosen here

1. **State the discipline where seats read it** — cite by content in a card (a quoted distinctive
   string, a symbol name, a test name) exactly as #11 requires in source. Costs nothing mechanical;
   relies on habit, which is what the three instances above already falsified once each.
2. **Extend #11's carrier list to card bodies** and say so in the commandment. ⚠️ That is an edit to a
   **governed surface** and therefore the skills seat's plus the maintainer's, ⛔ not this seat's —
   which is why it is offered rather than proposed.
3. **Make it falsifiable.** A PM-side check that, when a card is claimed, re-derives any `path:line`
   in its body and reports the ones that no longer land on what they claim. ⚠️ Needs a way to say
   what an address 「claims」, which is the hard half and may not be worth it.

⚠️ ⛔ One thing this card does NOT say: that the seats who wrote those addresses were careless. All
three cards' substantive readings held; it was the pointer that rotted. The instance on objectui#9899
was caught and published by the triage seat that had written it — which is the loop working, and the
reason this is a mechanism finding rather than a performance one.

Dedupe words: `line address in issue body` · `commandment 11 carrier list card` ·
`check-new-line-citations source only` · `stale file:line in card` · `cite by content in cards`
